newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: PIMCO eyes Asia fixed income asset growth.
newsitem.headline: PIMCO eyes Asia fixed income asset growth.

text.p: U.S-based Pacific Investment Management Company (PIMCO) could be directly managing fixed income investments in Asia within a few years, chief executive William S. Thomson said on Wednesday.
"I would guess in the next couple of years we could see ourselves taking positions, managing money offshore somewhere, outside of the U.S.," he told a news conference.

Part of PIMCO Advisors L.P. listed on the New York Stock Exchange -- the fourth largest publicly-listed fund management company in the United States -- PIMCO established its first overseas office in Singapore last October.
It does not yet manage fund money, but it opened the office to meet increasing demand for client liaison and marketing, research and portfolio management, Thomson said.
Some of its investments are handled through partnership with Pacific Asset Management Pte Ltd, set up earlier this year to serve institutional Asian and U.S. investors.
PIMCO acquired a 49 percent stake in Pacific Management, which also specialises in fixed income and currency fund management, but with emphasis on Southeast Asian markets.
"Their focus, just like ours, is fixed income. Long-term focus is on institutional and professional investors," Thomson said.
The alliance was mutually beneficial as PIMCO can gain more information about Asia's markets and access to new clients and direct more U.S. funds to this region, he said.
PIMCO manages mostly fixed income assets valued at US$90 billion, including bonds in three to four Asian markets.
Clients include central banks, government agencies, pensions, multi-national and insurance companies.
Thomson said there was a high probability PIMCO would seek to open another Asian office to tap capital flows linked to China and the rest of Asia, but did not elaborate.
He cited growth and diversity of these economies, high rates of savings, liberalisation and more market transparency as plus factors for PIMCO's interest in Asia.
Of PIMCO's US$90 billion in assets, about US$6-7 billion is invested in foreign bonds, Thomson said.
About US$3.5 billion is managed for Asian investors and US$1.5 billion for Singapore investors, he said.
Asked for his view on U.S. interest rate trends for the next six months, Thomson said the U.S. Federal Reserve's recent tightening could be the first of a series of further hikes.
"We believe the move was a pre-emptive move, one that really follows on the heels of the exuberance and concerns about the stock market, and tighter labour markets in the U.S." he said.
The Federal Funds rate was raised on March 25 by a quarter percent to 5.50 percent.
